entry.title: How to Check a Palindrome in Python
entry.summary:
A palindrome is a word, number, or sentence that reads the same forward and backward. For example: madam → madam
level → level
121 → 121
racecar → racecar
In this blog, we will learn how to check whether a word is a palindrome using Python. word = input("Enter a word: ")
reverse = word[::-1]
if word == reverse: print("It is a palindrome") else: print("It is not a palindrome")
word = input("Enter a word: ")
This asks the user to enter a word. For example: Enter a word: madam
reverse = word[::-1]
[::-1] is used to reverse a string. For example: madam → madam hello → olleh
if word == reverse:
The program checks whether the original word and reversed word are the same. If they are the same, it is a palindrome. print("It is a palindrome")
If the word is a palindrome, the program prints: It is a palindrome
Otherwise: It is not a palindrome
Enter a word: level
It is a palindrome
Another example: Enter a word: python
It is not a palindrome
Checking a palindrome is a simple and useful Python exercise. It helps beginners understand: Strings User input String slicing if-else conditions Comparing values

entry.title: How to Use a LinkedIn CV generator and What transfers to a Resume
entry.summary:
How to Convert Your LinkedIn Profile into an ATS-Friendly Resume
A LinkedIn CV generator can give you a draft, but a LinkedIn profile does not transfer cleanly into a resume. LinkedIn's PDF export can truncate sections, cannot be edited or tailored, and is not built for ATS parsing. The golden rule: Import the facts, then rebuild the document for the vacancy. Dedicated tools like PFPMaker can handle the photo, but they cannot handle the writing. Treat LinkedIn as a source record, not a document template. Strongest material: The underlying employment history, dates, education, skills, and contact details. Weakest material: The presentation—a public-facing headline, a long "About" section, and a layout chosen by LinkedIn. A good conversion keeps the evidence and discards the interface. …
